issues.description: Nil/IsZero guards copy-pasted across ~20 accessors instead of a single helper
issues.detail: The same `var s []T; if x != nil { s = x.field }; return seq.NewFixedSlice(s, ...)` boilerplate recurs across ir_file.go, ir_type.go, and ir_imports.go. One missed guard reintroduces a panic. Capture the invariant once — a zeroSafeSlice helper or a nil-tolerant seq.NewFixedSlice — so future accessors cannot drift.

issues.description: Zero-value contract is implicit and only enforced by a reflective test
issues.detail: Every accessor on a zero/nil receiver is supposed to return the zero of its result, but the contract is nowhere written down. State it once in package-level doc (or on IsZero) so future methods know the precondition. The test approximates the spec rather than codifying it.

issues.description: Two parallel zero predicates (f == nil vs x.IsZero()) for the same notion of absence
issues.detail: File uses `if f != nil` while Type/Member/Oneof/Element use `!x.IsZero()`. Different idioms for the same abstract guard invite drift and make future accessors inconsistent. Pick one canonical predicate across the IR types — ideally IsZero on *File too — so substitution is uniform.

issues.description: ValueNodeIndex returns sentinel -1, inventing a new postcondition callers will violate
issues.detail: Every other zero accessor returns the type's zero; ValueNodeIndex returns -1, and callers doing `MessageKeys().At(e.ValueNodeIndex())` will panic. The doc comment is not the type signature. Return `(int, bool)`, add a HasValueNode predicate, or require callers to check IsZero first.

issues.description: Reflective zero test silently skips methods with parameters and special-cases ad hoc
issues.detail: testZeroAny filters to NumIn()==1, so accessors taking arguments (e.g. ImportFor) never exercise the zero path, and Context/IsZero/ValueNodeIndex are special-cased inline. Add an explicit allowlist of skipped methods so new accessors cannot silently escape coverage.

issues.description: imports.Directs/Transitive closures still capture i and read i.publicEnd after the nil guard
issues.detail: When i==nil the empty slice prevents the mapper from running, so it works today. But the closure still references i.publicEnd / i.weakEnd, so any refactor that loses the length guard reintroduces the panic. Bail out earlier with an empty Indexer or assert non-nil at the top.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR identifies a real class of bug — accessors panicking on zero values — but resolves it by scattering ad-hoc nil/IsZero guards across roughly twenty call sites instead of capturing the invariant in one helper. The zero-value contract is sound in intent but implicit in execution: it lives only in a reflective test rather than stated in package doc, and two parallel predicates (`f == nil` vs `IsZero()`) coexist for the same notion. ValueNodeIndex's -1 sentinel is an abstraction leak that relocates the panic to callers. Land the test first, factor the guard into one helper, document the contract, and fix the sentinel before merging.
